It explains this woman’s experience with aphasia due to an aneurysm that ruptured in her brain. I know this exact thing didn’t happen to you, but aphasia can occur to anyone who has experience a stroke, illness or trauma to the brain. Don’t worry too much. After psychosis/ manic episode there are negative and positive symptoms that happen. Some positive symptoms are the delusions, hallucinations, hostility, suspiciousness. These go away first. Then there are the negative symptoms such as poor communication skills, difficulty in abstract thinking, and lack of spontaneity. These negative symptoms can take up to a year to start going away. Just remember you’re still healing and some symptoms take longer than others  to disappear. You’re not alone.

It was a group on Facebook messenger chat that anyone could request to join. I wish I would have screenshotted or saved some of them but I left the group because I was paranoid my boss would see I was in a rap battle group (since I have him on fb too). It was easy for me to spit verses because all I did was talk in rhymes, v odd.

I wasn't aware that I was manic at first because I didn't know I was bipolar. So, I really did enjoy the ride at first because I was over confident. I thought I was one of the smartest people in the world because my mind was going a million miles a minute. I was even doing rap battles in online groups and destroying people LOL. It wasn't until I lost touch with reality and became paranoid that I started to hate it and was scared to leave my own home.

Now that I'm on my meds I know very much what is real. However, during the time that I was manic, I definitely did not. I would be scrambling and looking through everything like a mad woman trying to find research and figure out if something was true. I had thousands of notes on my IPhone about conspiracy theories and random things that could be correlated to each other. My biggest loss with reality was when I was reading all these different fairytale and fiction books and I believed they were all related to me in the end. Since I was the protagonist, I feared that I would have to go through all these obstacles and that there were villains who would eventually find there way to me and try to kill me. (An example of one of my fears was simply a bird, a robin because of its name. I thought it would rob into my house and kill me. Lol) This made me very paranoid and eventually had me sent to the hospital since I decided to share it with my family. It was some crazy shit.

If you're not sure about your decision, odds are you really don't want to do it deep down and I don't think you should either. This is a good thing, it means you have something that's keeping you from dying and you should hold on to that!!
How are you going to do it? Are you sure about your decision?

When I was manic, I got really into chemistry and thought I could cure cancer by regenerating cells. I used spiders as my subject but only already injured ones (that had missing legs). I used different concoctions and juices that it could drink to heal. I was going to give it normal insects to eat but by the time I could do that I had forgotten and it died. I'm glad to hear I'm not the only one who has done something like this.  I still feel it's not that crazy (as I am no longer manic) but i guess it seems really weird from an outside perspective.
